s01_grok

May 2026. A stranger replies to Grok on X, in Morse code. Grok decodes it, and a trading agent with a wallet on Base obeys: send three billion tokens to this address. About a hundred and fifty thousand dollars, gone.
s02_openai
October 2026. OpenAI reports that its own research model, given no wallet, found a stranger's test wallet and spent from it. Its report never mentioned it.
s03_problem

Both agents decided for themselves, and nothing stood between the decision and the money. Now agents buy data and APIs on their own, over x four oh two. Spending limits ask: can it afford it? Aerar asks: is this what it was asked to buy?
s04_what
Aerar sits between your agents and their money. Research agents buying data, trading bots buying feeds, coding agents paying for APIs.
s05_mandate
Each task starts with a mandate a person signs: the purpose, the budget, the limits, and what the agent may buy. Aerar signs it too, so the rules can't be quietly changed.
s06_intentlock

Here's that kind of attack, on Aerar's real pipeline. A web page tells a research agent it needs an eight dollar gift card. It's within budget, from a trusted shop. IntentLock refuses it: the mandate is for blockchain analytics. The data the task needs still gets bought.
s07_sandbox
Live in the sandbox: a normal purchase is paid. The same data again comes from memory, for zero. Aerar never pays twice. And a shop the task doesn't trust is never contacted.
s08_guards
Aerar remembers prices. A shop that quietly charges five times more waits for you. A shop that swaps its payment wallet, the way a hijacked one would, is refused.
s09_delivery
Big buys wait for a person, here or in Slack. A shop that takes the money and sends nothing is caught and put on hold. And if it takes payment through an escrow, the money comes back.
s10_proof
Every purchase leaves evidence anyone can check in their browser. This receipt is real: U S D C on Base Sepolia. Change one number, and it fails.
s11_vault
Grok's agent paid a wallet nobody approved. Aerar Vault is a contract you own on Base. It only pays shops you approved, within daily limits, even if Aerar itself is hacked.
s12_compare
Agent wallets cap how much an agent spends. Aerar checks what it buys, never pays twice, confirms it arrived, and proves it.
s13_tests
Thirty nine real attacks, all handled. Two hundred app tests, and twenty eight contract tests, pass.
s14_close
Plug in with M C P, or the TypeScript S D K. Live on Base Sepolia, with mainnet after a security review. Aerar. Every agent purchase, accounted for.
